methodological_rigor.justification: The study deploys a multi-modal experimental strategy: serum ELISA (OGN, estradiol, ADAM12), MRE of PDAC tumors (n=11), multiple human and murine scRNA-seq datasets, microdissected proteomics, patient-derived organoid-fibroblast cocultures (BJ, MEFs, PS-1, P361, P371 CAFs, P411/P067 organoids), lentiviral shRNA knockdowns (Clec3b with 5 clones, CLEC3B with 4 clones, SLC25A44 with 5 clones), PDX sections, and LC/MS-MS quantification of tissue estrogens with stable-isotope internal standards. Multivariable Cox regression is used in the CPCT-02 cohort to correct for PDAC subtypes. Weaknesses include small MRE cohort (n=11), reliance on correlative associations across several public datasets, heterogeneous shRNA-KD phenotypic effects (acknowledged), and lack of in vivo causal perturbation of aromatase or SLC25A44. Statistical reporting is adequate (t-test, Mann-Whitney, ANOVA, log-rank, correlation) but with limited correction for multiple testing beyond Bonferroni in the scRNA-seq differential expression.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work reframes PDAC stromal biology by proposing PDAC-intrinsic estrogen synthesis (via aromatase and BCAA-fueled precursors) that shapes tumor-suppressive CLEC3B+ iCAF phenotypes and epithelial-like molecular subtypes. This has clear translational implications: CLEC3B and estrogen-biosynthesis signatures are independently prognostic in metastatic PDAC (CPCT-02), and aromatase/SLC25A44 become candidate biomarkers or targets that caution against broad estrogen-pathway inhibition in PDAC. As a basic/mechanistic study combining patient samples with in vitro and in silico analyses, Oxford LoE is 5.

reporting_quality.justification: No single standard from the prespecified list cleanly applies; the most relevant mix is ARRIVE (for any in vivo PDX/KPC elements) and REMARK-like reporting for prognostic biomarkers, so 'other' is most appropriate. Methods are richly detailed (antibody RRIDs, primer sequences, software versions, MRE protocols, LC-MS transitions). Publicly referenced datasets (PXD011289, E-MTAB-6830, CRA001160, CPCT-02 via Hartwig) are cited, and multivariable Cox output is reported in supplementary material. Data availability is reasonable for a mechanistic paper but newly generated in-house datasets (MRE, ELISA, LC-MS, shRNA-KD FACS) do not have explicit repository deposits visible in the text.

novelty_literature.justification: The central finding - that PDAC epithelial cells synthesize estrogen de novo, with intratumoral estradiol concentrations (~2,193 pmol/L) exceeding postmenopausal serum references, fueled by CAF-derived BCAA catabolism through SLC25A44 - is mechanistically novel and contradicts the default assumption that PDAC is hormonally inert. The linkage of estrogen-signaling to an OGN/CLEC3B-marked iCAF.1 subset with independent prognostic value across multiple cohorts (including CPCT-02 metastatic PDAC) is also new. While individual elements (sex disparities in PDAC, BCAA metabolism in PDAC stroma) have prior literature, the integrated hormone-stroma circuit is a first-in-class proposal.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear narrative arc: sex dimorphism in stroma -> estrogen signaling -> CLEC3B-driven CAF phenotype -> intratumoral estrogen synthesis -> BCAA-fueled biosynthesis pathway. Figures integrate serum, imaging (MRE), bulk/single-cell transcriptomics, IHC, LC/MS-MS, and in vitro perturbation. Methods are thorough. Minor weaknesses include dense methods paragraphs, occasional awkward phrasing, and complex figure legends requiring careful reading.

key_strengths: Novel mechanistic discovery that PDAC epithelial cells produce estrogen de novo, with intratumoral estradiol measured by LC/MS-MS exceeding postmenopausal serum reference values

Integration of serum biomarkers, MRE tissue stiffness, multi-cohort transcriptomics (TCGA, CPCT-02 metastatic, microdissected, single-cell), and in vitro perturbation to support a coherent hormone-stroma-subtype axis
Identification of CLEC3B/tetranectin as an estrogen-target CAF marker that is independently prognostic across resectable and metastatic PDAC cohorts

Mechanistic linkage of CAF-derived BCAA metabolism (via SLC25A44) to steroid hormone precursor production, with functional knockdown validation that shifts PDAC cells toward basal/mesenchymal phenotypes
key_concerns: Small MRE cohort (n=11) and uneven sample sizes in LC/MS-MS and ELISA validation cohorts limit precision of sex-based differences
No in vivo causal perturbation of aromatase (CYP19A1) or SLC25A44 in PDAC models to directly test the proposed estrogen-synthesis axis
Heterogeneous shRNA-KD effects on STAT3 phosphorylation and iCAF/myCAF markers suggest context-dependence that is not fully mechanistically dissected
No explicit data availability statement for newly generated datasets (MRE, LC/MS-MS, FACS, qRT-PCR) beyond public dataset citations
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-impact, mechanistically novel study with multimodal evidence supporting PDAC-intrinsic estrogen synthesis shaping a tumor-suppressive stroma; suitable for a Tier 1 venue such as Cancer Discovery or Nature Cancer pending in vivo causal validation of aromatase/SLC25A44.
